question: to the Commission Catherine Griset (PfE) Subject:

The streamer Ultia was removed from the committee for CNC Talent – a fund supporting video creators within the framework of the National Centre for Cinema and the Moving Image – following her revelations about favouritism displayed by committee members towards creators cut from the same ideological cloth as them. Thus it follows that the fund, which provides grants for both fictional works and documentaries on YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Twitch, could end up being hijacked to the benefit of left-wing activists, despite the inclusion of the principles of impartiality and neutrality in the CNC’s General Framework for Funding. The fund’s yearly budget of EUR 3 million comes from the CNC’s general budget, which is financed through taxes on: - cinema tickets (10.72 % of cost price); - television services; - the dissemination of physical videos (DVD, Blu-ray) or online videos (streaming). Against this backdrop: 1.
Does the Commission fund CNC Talent, for example under the media strand of the Creative Europe programme?
If so, are the grants subject to ethical obligations, such as compliance with the principles of impartiality or neutrality?
Does the European Court of Auditors audit EU funds for online platform content creation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.6.2026) The MEDIA strand of the Creative Europe programme1 does not fund the National Centre of Cinema (CNC) Talent action2. More generally, MEDIA does not include an online platform content action like the CNC Talent action, which targets content produced by online creators with a significant presence on video-sharing platforms. When it comes to funding audiovisual content creation, the targeted beneficiaries of Creative Europe MEDIA funding are European independent audiovisual production companies, in line with the Creative Europe Regulation3. The definition of eligible production companies is not linked to a presence on video-sharing platforms. Most of the works supported for content creation under the Creative Europe MEDIA programme are intended primarily for cinema, followed by content made primarily for television. In light of the above, questions 2) and 3) do not arise in this specific case.
1 Regulation (eu) 2021/818 of the European parliament and of the Council of 20 May 2021establishing the

Creative Europe Programme (2021 to 2027). 2 Information accessed on 28 April 2026 from https://www.cnc.fr/professionnels/aides-et-financements/creationnumerique/fonds-daide-aux-createurs-video-sur-internet-cnc-talent_190814. 3 See for example sub-section a) and b) of Section 2 of Annex 1, Regulation above.
